title: Saying more with less — nominalisation and the effective sentence
goal: Build the *pe-an* and *per-an* nouns that give formal Indonesian its weight (*pelaksanaan, penerapan, peningkatan*), and then learn when to turn them back into verbs, so that your reports read like *kalimat efektif*: clear, short and free of spare parts.
bekal: turn a *me-* verb into its noun and back: *melaksanakan ↔ pelaksanaan*, *meningkatkan ↔ peningkatan*
cut the classic redundancies: *para peserta-peserta*, *sangat antusias sekali*, *meskipun … tetapi*
use *daripada* only where it belongs: *lebih baik daripada*, *daripada menunggu*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Laporan yang berbelit-belit
dialogs.intro: Tuesday, 16 January 2029. The programme's first activity report is due to the board on Monday. Yoga, the UGM intern from the Sumberwangi project and now a junior staffer at Program Jembatan, wrote the draft; Sarah goes through it with him in the meeting room.

lines.text: Yoga, kalimat pertamamu ini empat baris. Coba kita baca bareng.
lines.id: Yoga, this first sentence of yours is four lines long. Let's read it together.
lines.literal: Yoga, sentence first-your this four line. try we read together.

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Iya, Mbak. Biar kelihatan formal, gitu.
lines.id: Yes. So it looks formal, you know.
lines.literal: yes, Miss. so-that looks formal, like-that.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: ‘Para peserta-peserta program sangat antusias sekali.’ Ada yang aneh?

lines.literal: ‘[para] participant-participant programme very enthusiastic very.’ exist that odd?

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Hmm… ‘para’ sama ‘peserta-peserta’ dobel, ya?
lines.id: Hmm… ‘para’ and ‘peserta-peserta’ double up, don't they?
lines.literal: hmm… ‘para’ with ‘participant-participant’ double, [ya]?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Betul. ‘Para’ sudah jamak. ‘Sangat’ dan ‘sekali’ juga jangan dipakai berdua.
lines.id: Right. ‘Para’ is already plural. And don't use ‘sangat’ and ‘sekali’ together either.
lines.literal: correct. ‘para’ already plural. ‘very’ and ‘very’ also don't be-used as-two.

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Jadi, ‘Para peserta program sangat antusias.’ Oke, lebih pendek.
lines.id: So: ‘The programme participants were very enthusiastic.’ OK, shorter.
lines.literal: so, ‘[para] participant programme very enthusiastic.’ OK, more short.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Terus ini: ‘Daripada itu, kami melakukan pelaksanaan kegiatan pelatihan guru.’
lines.id: Then this: ‘Than that, we carried out the implementation of teacher-training activities.’
lines.literal: then this: ‘than that, we do implementation activity training teacher.’

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Salahnya di mana, Mbak? Kedengarannya pinter.
lines.id: What's wrong with it? It sounds clever.
lines.literal: wrong-its at where, Miss? sound-its clever.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: ‘Daripada’ itu untuk membandingkan. Dan ‘melakukan pelaksanaan’ sama saja dengan ‘melaksanakan’.
lines.id: ‘Daripada’ is for comparing. And ‘melakukan pelaksanaan’ is just ‘melaksanakan’.
lines.literal: ‘than’ that for compare. and ‘do implementation’ same just with ‘implement’.

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Berarti cukup ‘Selain itu, kami melaksanakan pelatihan guru’?
lines.id: So just ‘Besides that, we ran teacher training’?
lines.literal: means enough ‘besides that, we implement training teacher’?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Nah, itu kalimat efektif. Subjeknya jelas, kata kerjanya satu.
lines.id: There you go, that's an effective sentence. Clear subject, one verb.
lines.literal: [nah], that sentence effective. subject-its clear, word work-its one.

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Tapi kata dosen saya, laporan harus pakai banyak kata benda.
lines.id: But my lecturer said reports should use lots of nouns.
lines.literal: but word lecturer my, report must use many word thing.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Boleh, asal ada gunanya. ‘Peningkatan Mutu Guru’ bagus sebagai judul.
lines.id: Fine, as long as they do a job. ‘Improving Teacher Quality’ works well as a heading.
lines.literal: may, provided exist use-its. ‘increase quality teacher’ good as title.

lines.speaker: Yoga:
lines.text: Siap, Mbak. Aku pangkas semua. Lihat coretan sebanyak ini, aku auto insecure.
lines.id: Right. I'll trim the lot. Seeing this much red ink, I'm instantly insecure.
lines.literal: ready, Miss. I trim all. see cross-out as-many this, I auto insecure.

notes: **Para peserta-peserta** is a double plural. *Para* marks a group of people (*para guru, para tamu*), and doubling the noun marks the plural too, so one of them must go: *para peserta* or *peserta-peserta*, never both. The same goes for numbers and *banyak*: *tiga buku*, *banyak buku*, not *tiga buku-buku*.

**Sangat antusias sekali** stacks two words for “very”. *Sangat* goes before the adjective and *sekali* after it; choose one. *Amat* is a third, slightly literary option, and *banget* is its spoken cousin, which does not belong in a report either.

**Daripada itu** is not Indonesian for “moreover”. *Daripada* means “than” or “rather than”, and nothing else. Its misuse as an all-purpose connector was so typical of New Order officials' speeches that it became a standing joke; Sarah's fix, *Selain itu*, is what the sentence actually means.

**Melakukan pelaksanaan** — “to do the carrying-out”. It is a verb turned into a noun and then propped up with an empty verb. If a proper verb exists, use it: *melaksanakan*. Some *melakukan* + noun pairs are accepted (*melakukan penelitian, melakukan kunjungan*), but the plain verb is always shorter.

**Biar, gitu, bareng, pinter — Yoga's register.** *Biar* = *agar/supaya* (so that), *gitu* = *begitu*, *bareng* = *bersama*, *pinter* = *pintar*. *Auto insecure* is pure Gen-Z: *auto* means “instantly, automatically”, and English emotional words like *insecure* and *overthinking* are borrowed wholesale.

**Memangkas** — “to trim, prune”, from *pangkas*. Barbers *memangkas rambut*, governments *memangkas anggaran* (cut the budget), and editors *memangkas kalimat*. *Coretan* (from *coret*, “cross out”) is the red ink itself.

grammars.title: Nominalisation: from verb to noun
body: Formal Indonesian loves nouns built with *pe-an* and *per-an*; they give reports, headlines and titles their weight. As a rule, a *me-* verb gives a *pe-an* noun, and a *ber-* verb often gives a *per-an* noun.
after: The sound changes are the same as in the verb: *laksana → melaksanakan → pelaksanaan*, *terap → menerapkan → penerapan*, *tingkat → meningkatkan → peningkatan*. If you can build the verb, you can build the noun.

⚠️ Nouns are for headings, titles and subjects: *Peningkatan mutu guru menjadi prioritas kami.* When a noun merely sits after an empty verb (*melakukan peningkatan*), turn it back into a verb: *meningkatkan*.

grammars.title: The effective sentence: six cuts
body: *Kalimat efektif* is the schoolbook term for a sentence with no spare parts. Indonesian teachers check three things: a clear subject and predicate, no redundancy, and one connector per link.
after: The preposition trap is the one that fails exams. A sentence that opens with *Bagi…*, *Dalam…* or *Kepada…* turns its subject into a prepositional phrase and leaves the sentence with no subject at all. Drop the preposition, or supply a real subject.
⚠️ One connector per link: *meskipun … tetapi*, *walaupun … namun* and *karena … maka* are errors in written Indonesian, even though you will hear them in every meeting.

dialogs.title: Second dialogue — Terlalu panjang, Sarah
dialogs.intro: Friday, 19 January. Pak Hendra, Sarah's old boss from her first year in Jakarta and now the director she reports to, has read the revised report. He calls her from his office on a video call.

lines.speaker: Hendra:
lines.text: Sarah, laporannya sudah jauh lebih baik. Tapi masih terlalu panjang.
lines.id: Sarah, the report is far better now. But it's still too long.
lines.literal: Sarah, report-the already far more good. but still too long.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Idealnya berapa halaman, Pak?
lines.id: How many pages would be ideal?
lines.literal: ideal-its how-many page, Sir?

lines.speaker: Hendra:
lines.text: Dewan direksi hanya membaca halaman pertama. Jadi, ringkasan eksekutif maksimal satu halaman.
lines.id: The board only reads the first page. So the executive summary is one page at most.
lines.literal: council directors only read page first. so, summary executive maximum one page.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Baik. Isinya cukup tiga hal: pelaksanaan, hasil, dan rencana?
lines.id: Right. Then three things are enough: what we did, results and plans?
lines.literal: good. content-its enough three thing: implementation, result, and plan?

lines.speaker: Hendra:
lines.text: Tepat. Dan hindari kalimat seperti ‘Adapun pelaksanaan kegiatan tersebut adalah sebagai berikut.’
lines.id: Exactly. And avoid sentences like ‘As regards the implementation of the said activities, it is as follows.’
lines.literal: exact. and avoid sentence like ‘as-for implementation activity the-said is as following.’

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Itu kalimat Yoga, Pak. Dia bangga sekali dengan kalimat itu.
lines.id: That's Yoga's sentence. He's very proud of it.
lines.literal: that sentence Yoga, Sir. he proud very with sentence that.

lines.speaker: Hendra:
lines.text: Hahaha. Tulis saja ‘Kegiatannya sebagai berikut.’ Selesai.
lines.id: Ha! Just write ‘The activities were as follows.’ Done.
lines.literal: hahaha. write just ‘activity-the as following.’ finished.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Angka-angkanya saya pindahkan ke lampiran, Pak?
lines.id: Shall I move the figures to the appendix?
lines.literal: number-number-the I move to appendix, Sir?

lines.speaker: Hendra:
lines.text: Ya, kecuali satu: jumlah guru yang sudah dilatih. Itu harus di depan.
lines.id: Yes, except one: the number of teachers already trained. That has to be up front.
lines.literal: yes, except one: amount teacher that already be-trained. that must at front.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Siap, Pak. Senin pagi versi ringkasnya sudah ada di meja Bapak.
lines.id: Will do. The short version will be on your desk on Monday morning.
lines.literal: ready, Sir. Monday morning version concise-its already exist at desk Sir.

notes: **Jauh lebih baik** — “far better”. *Jauh* (far) intensifies a comparative, the way English uses “far” or “much”. Its opposite is *sedikit lebih* (a little more): *sedikit lebih pendek*, a bit shorter.

**Ringkasan eksekutif** — “executive summary”. *Ringkas* means concise; *ringkasan* is a summary and *meringkas* is to summarise. *Versi ringkas* is “the short version”, and Pak Hendra will ask for one every time.

**Adapun … adalah sebagai berikut.** *Adapun* is a formal topic marker, “as for”, and *tersebut* is the official “the said, the aforementioned”. Both have their place in legal and ministerial writing, but stacked together at the start of a report they are pure throat-clearing.
**Bangga sekali** — *sekali* on its own is perfectly correct; the problem in Yoga's sentence was stacking it with *sangat*. *Bangga dengan* or *bangga akan* means “proud of”.

**Lampiran** — “appendix, attachment”, from *lampir*. *Melampirkan* is to attach, and *terlampir* means “attached”: *Berkas terlampir* (file attached) is how thousands of Indonesian emails end. You will build formal letters around this word in Unit 3.
**Di meja Bapak** — “on your desk”. To a superior, *Bapak* replaces *Anda* completely. Sarah speaks baku to Pak Hendra, but warmly; he calls her plain *Sarah*, as a senior may.

grammars.title: Cutting the filler: pairs that do one job
body: Pak Hendra's rule is every Indonesian editor's rule: if two words do one job, one of them goes. Most of the bloat in formal Indonesian comes from pairs like these.

head: Filler
Meaning
Keep only
rows: as for …, it is as follows

after: *Hanya … saja* is so common in speech that nobody minds it there. In writing, keep one of the two.

Headings stay nominal (*Pelaksanaan Kegiatan*, *Rencana Tindak Lanjut*); the sentences under them should be built on verbs. Nouns on top and verbs below is most of what makes an Indonesian report readable.

blocks.text: The same pattern produces most of the vocabulary of a report. Read across: root, verb, noun.

⚠️ *Pelatihan* is training, a workshop, a course: *pelatihan guru*. *Latihan* is an exercise or practice: what you will do at the end of this unit, or what a football team does on Tuesday evenings. Mixing them up is a very common learner error.

*Daripada* has two honest jobs: “than” after *lebih* or *kurang*, and “rather than” at the head of a sentence. Everything else is decoration borrowed from old-style officialese, and editors strike it out.
In speech, Indonesians often say *dari* for “than”: *lebih besar dari itu*. It is heard everywhere and KBBI accepts it, but careful writers and exam markers prefer *daripada* in comparisons.
Cover the Indonesian column, read the English, and rebuild each sentence from memory.

head: English
Indonesian
rows: Go ahead, Sarah. Imagine I'm the Bupati.
*Silakan mulai, Mbak Sarah. Anggap saja saya Pak Bupati.*
*Memaparkan.* Right, I'll note that. Then, first of all, I explain the background.
*Memaparkan. Baik, saya catat. Lalu pertama-tama saya jelaskan latar belakangnya.*
Now that's convincing. Next, the challenges and plans for the future. Not just the pretty things.
*Nah, itu meyakinkan. Selanjutnya, tantangan dan rencana ke depan. Jangan hanya yang indah-indah.*
Perfect. But have an answer ready in case Pak Harun asks about next year's funding.
*Sempurna. Tapi siapkan juga jawaban kalau Pak Harun bertanya soal dana tahun depan.*
